findings.title: Neither authority path §4.3 names for the reviewed-plan blob proof exists in the schema, so the R1 alignment fix is unbuildable as written and degrades back to the hole it replaces
findings.detail: §4.3 correctly identifies the defect and correctly forbids the unsafe binding ('A same-execution/current manifest without proof that it belongs to that request is insufficient'), but both authority sources it prescribes are unavailable against today's tables. (1) 'a manifest durably bound to that exact approved request/revision': design_review_manifest.request_id is a randomUUID() minted inside advanceDesignReviewManifest (StateStore.ts:16903-16914) and is the inbox instruction id, NOT codex_review_job.request_id (StateStore.ts:7800-7812, PK from the review coordinator). No column on either table references the other; the only join is execution_id plus the MUTABLE is_current pointer, which is exactly what readShipJudgmentPlanReference (StateStore.ts:5756) and EvidenceAuthorityReader.designApproval (evidence-authority.ts:70-84) use today. The one place the reviewed blob is actually checked, POST /design-review-validation (design-review-validation.ts:48-100, wired at plugin.ts:2724-2741), is stateless: it returns {allowed:true} and persists nothing, so after acceptance no row records which manifest revision/blob the APPROVED verdict validated. (2) 'that approved request's immutable frozen_head_sha': review-request-coordinator.ts:920-931 derives and freezes a head ONLY when reviewType === 'code'; design registrations pass frozenHeadSha undefined into insertCodexReviewJob (coordinator:1055-1067, StateStore.ts:17752-17770), so codex_review_job.frozen_head_sha is NULL for every design job. The sole design path that ever stamps it is the reuse-release branch (coordinator:1948-1952) which writes the head at RELEASE time — not the reviewed commit. §4.3 presents this path as the one that 'supports Codex-author reviews without a matching Claude manifest', i.e. precisely the population it was added to serve, and that claim is false against the code. §4.3 also does not list any schema addition or implementation task to create the missing binding: §2's new row and §7 task 1 only say to implement §4.3 in evidence-authority/evidence-ledger/production-collect. Add the missing durable record (e.g. persist the validated manifest revision + expected_blob_sha, or the resolved reviewed commit, onto the design review job or a new design_review_approval_proof row at the moment /design-review-validation accepts), state the policy for historical approvals that have no such proof, and list it as its own task — otherwise the two positive cases §4.3's closing paragraph demands cannot be written.
findings.failure_scenario: Implement reaches task 1 and finds no way to satisfy §4.3's reviewed-plan proof: every design job has frozen_head_sha NULL and no manifest row is bound to the approved request. Either (a) it implements the rule literally, every target gets missing(alignment,'reviewed_plan_blob'), alignment is permanently undetermined in both modes, the card shows ① 待补证 forever and auto approval can never fire — the 'permanently inert' outcome §4.3's own last paragraph forbids; or (b), to make the required positive case green, it falls back to getCurrentDesignReviewManifest(execution_id) — the mutable is_current join §4.3 declares insufficient. Under (b) a runner runs `stage set design_review --plan` after its APPROVED verdict, advanceDesignReviewManifest flips is_current and records the NEW blob, evidence-authority attaches that new expectedBlobSha, production-collect reads the edited plan at head, the SHAs match, alignment passes, and the widened auto writer merges a PR whose design authority is bytes no reviewer ever saw — the original R1 HIGH, restored.

findings.title: Making an explicit semantic alignment=pass AND coverage=pass mandatory adds a second, undisclosed single point of inertness on the model lane
findings.detail: This change is the right safety fix — applySemanticEvidence (evidence-ledger.ts:427-454) is veto-only today, so an 'undetermined' semantic result leaves a deterministic pass standing, and §4.3 correctly closes that. But it also converts the model from a veto into a NECESSARY condition for merge authority, and evaluate.ts:118-170 rejects to invalid(...) on a wide surface (alignment_evidence_missing, coverage_evidence_missing, use_case_duplicate, implementation_evidence_missing, use_case_missing, coverage_result_inconsistent, test_evidence_missing, exemption_scope_missing, test_reference_unverified), any of which now blocks approval outright. §10's R2 paragraph and acceptance row V disclose only the GitHub collection-capacity precondition (120 reservations/hour in project-refresh.ts:423-443 plus the 60s cache lifetime at :568-580); neither mentions model-lane availability. When the Codex account pool is exhausted or the evaluator returns schema-imperfect output, the feature is silently inert for a second, unrelated reason. Fail-closed, so not ship-blocking, but it belongs in the same precondition/limitation section as the budget item and in row V's measurement, and the founder page's §08 limitation sentence currently names only the request quota.
findings.failure_scenario: Collection capacity is healthy and row V passes, but the model lane is degraded (quota exhausted, or the evaluator emits output that trips one of evaluate.ts's invalid() branches on most cards). Every card renders 缺证据, no approval ever fires, and operators reading §10/row V conclude the budget precondition was met and look for a collection bug that does not exist.
